doc.title: Peter Vacher interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 18, 2001

title: Musician feedback and the singer-wife problem
summary: Musicians like Alan Ganley phone with reactions; reviewing a musician whose wife sings can be awkward.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Critics, polls and the jazz press

blocks.x: You anticipated a question I had.
Like how many times have you gotten feedback?
Do you get positive feedback too?

Yes. It is pleasing if a musician makes the point. Alan Ganley for instance, who I’ve known Gan many years, unfailingly courteous. And I mean I quite often review his big band. He has a rather fine big band. He would always telephone. And that’s very nice. It’s courteous and there’s a sense of it being something we’re both in together. I mean I feel I’m part of it in the sense that I’m trying to support it if you follow me. Other musicians have dropped me a line or rung me up and said look, you’ve got it right man, which is a pleasing reaction. Very occasionally someone will say hmmm, not too sure about your comments there. And you realize that you’ve just stepped a little bit towards a nerve. And I mean there’s a couple of musicians, I won’t name names, in Britain, whose wives are singers. Well they are fine players. They also have wives who are singers. Are you following my drift?

But the problem is to have him, you must have her. And there’s one I know very, very well who, he’s really quite a good friend. And if I don’t praise his wife, wow. And I don’t want to praise her because frankly she’s not of the same caliber as her husband. So that can be a little bit sticky.
